title: Chromatin-associated protein networks of CEBPA and SUMO2/3 identified with RIME
projectDescription: We identified the chromatin-associated protein networks of CEBPA and SUMO2/3 in BLaER1 cells during the early stages of B-cell-to-macrophage transdifferentiation. Additionally, we studied the impact of SUMOylation inhibition (SUMOi) on CEBPA protein network composition utilizing the small molecule inhibitor ML-792. Protein network members were identified with Rapid Immunoprecipitation Mass spectrometry of Endogenous proteins (RIME) at 0, 6 and 24 h after induction of transdifferentiation in the absence and presence of ML-792. Mass spectrometry analyses were executed with high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-MS), using the Evosep One liquid chromatography system coupled to a hybrid trapped ion mobility quadrupole TOF mass spectrometer (Bruker timsTOF Pro) via a CaptiveSpray nano-electrospray ion source. High-confidence chromatome members were discriminated from background with SAINT analysis.
sampleProcessingProtocol: BLaER1 cells were seeded into 15 cm culture dishes at 15×10^6 cells per dish in maintenance medium as three biological replicates and transdifferentiation was induced by treating the cells with 100 nM beta-estradiol (E2) in the presence of 10 ng/ml hrIL-3 and 10 ng/ml hrCSF-1. In SUMOylation inhibition studies, cells were exposed to 100 nM ML-792 (SUMOi; MedKoo Biosciences, #407886) or an equivalent volume of DMSO for 24h prior to induction. Cells were harvested at 0, 6 and 24 h after induction. Crosslinking and cell lysate preparation were performed as previously described (doi: 10.1038/s41388-025-03305-3). Fragmented chromatin was incubated with specific antibody for CEBPA (purified rabbit IgG from Thomas Graf lab), SUMO2/3 (MBL, M114-3) or their IgG controls overnight (16 h) at 4°C, in a total volume of 1 ml RIME-RIPA buffer (prepared in LC-MS grade H2O). Antibody-coupled chromatin was captured to magnetic Protein G beads over 16 h at 4°C. Immunoprecipitated chromatin was then washed ten times with RIPA-buffer followed by two washes with 100 mM ammonium hydrogen carbonate (AMBIC). Beads were then flash frozen and peptide masses were analyzed with high resolution mass spectrometry (LC/LC-MS, Evosep) in Helsinki University Proteomics Unit. Enzymatic digestion, peptide de-salting by solid-phase extraction and LC-MS/MS were performed as described in the original RIME protocol (doi: 10.1038/nprot.2016.020). Briefly, beads were washed with AMBIC and sequencing grade modified trypsin was added to beads for 15 min with frequent vortexing and left for digestion overnight at 37°C without further agitation followed by added trypsin for 4 h. Peptide digests in supernatant were quenched with trifluoroacetic acid and finally desalted with C18 MicroSpin columns as previously described (doi: 10.1038/s41596-020-0365-x). The dried peptides were reconstituted in Buffer A, diluted 1:20 HPLC water containing formic acid and loaded onto Evotips (Evosec) by manufacturer’s instructions. LC-MS analysis was performed by using the Evosep One liquid chromatography system coupled to a hybrid trapped ion mobility quadrupole TOF mass spectrometer (Bruker timsTOF Pro) via a CaptiveSpray nano-electrospray ion source. Separation was done in 8 cm × 150 µm column with 1.5 µm C18 beads with 60 samples per day methods (21 min gradient time). Mobile phases A and B were 0.1 % formic acid in water and 0.1 % formic acid in acetonitrile, respectively. The MS analysis was performed in the positive-ion mode using data-dependent acquisition (DDA) in PASEF17 mode with DDA-PASEF-short_gradient_0.5s-cycletime -method.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data (.d) were processed with FragPipe v17.1 utilizing MSFragger18 against reviewed human entries of the UniProtKB database (downloaded 8.3.2022). Aminoterminal acetylation and oxidation of methionine were used as dynamic modification. Biotinylation of lysine and N-termini were set as variable modifications. Trypsin was selected as enzyme, and a maximum of two missed cleavages were allowed. Both instrument and label-free quantification parameters were left to default settings. Final results from these steps are Spectral Counts (SPC) values from peptides with FDR < 0.01 from Philosopher.
